rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable breast engorgement / Diagnose probable blocked milk duct / Diagnose probable mastitis associated with lactation / Diagnose probable mastalgia
rule_level_problems.problem: All four use (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Pain of breast" "finding")) as the 'painful breast/s' evidence. In SNOMED, 'Sore nipple' and 'Painful lactation' are direct children of 'Pain of breast', and descendants match in due_to. The page's left branch ('Breastfeeding and painful/cracked nipples') is deliberately separate from 'painful breast/s with or without lump/s', yet a breastfeeding patient recorded with sore nipples alone would receive probable engorgement and probable blocked duct (afebrile) or probable mastitis (febrile). Nothing in the file checks for or excludes nipple pain.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable breast abscess / Diagnose probable mastitis associated with lactation
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Body pain' is encoded as (snomed_concept "Generalized aches and pains" "finding"). The system's recorded common symptom for body/muscle pain is 'Muscle pain', which is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of 'Generalized aches and pains' (checked). A patient whose body pain is recorded as Muscle pain will fail the fever-or-body-pain test in both rules and, if breastfeeding and afebrile, fall through to probable engorgement/blocked duct instead of mastitis. Either add Muscle pain as an alternative or use the common-symptom concept.

The diagnosis concept (snomed_concept "Pain of breast" "finding") is identical to one of its own evidence findings, so the rule records as a probable diagnosis the very finding the nurse entered. Mastalgia is a SNOMED synonym of Pain of breast and no better general concept exists (Cyclical / Non-cyclical mastalgia are narrower than the page), so this may be the best available, but it should be flagged for the clinician.

summary: The red box is encoded correctly except that fluctuance is not checked for, and the Urgent priority is anchored to the probable abscess as the house pattern requires. The most consequential problem is that 'Pain of breast' silently absorbs sore/painful nipples through the SNOMED hierarchy, so the page's separate cracked-nipple branch is mis-diagnosed as engorgement/blocked duct or mastitis; the second is that body pain is encoded as 'Generalized aches and pains', which the recorded common symptom 'Muscle pain' does not match. The warning-signs screen (skin changes, nipple discharge/retraction, axillary lump, family history) is entirely absent from the file, which is arguably defensible since the page names no diagnosis and no matching priority level, but it leaves two of the page's five presenting complaints unrepresented.
